correctness.rationale: Exact monomial norms yield the reciprocal-moment diagonal kernel and Bergman curvature \(\operatorname{Var}(N)/r^2\). The strictly log-concave continuous moment integrand has a unique saddle \(q_t\), with \(B_t\sim2\alpha(\log t)^{\alpha-1}\to\infty\); local Gaussian Laplace expansion and concavity tail bounds give \(a'(t)\sim B_t/t\) and \(a''(t)\sim-B_t/t^2\). A discrete log-concave saddle at \(a'(t_x)=x\) has variance \(\sim 2\alpha x^{-2}(\log(1/x))^{\alpha-1}\), justified by Riemann-sum normal approximation and tangent-tail bounds. The metric coefficient \(\sqrt{2\alpha}\) follows since \(x\sim1-r^2\); rotational invariance and radial path minimization *within the axis* yield the length coefficient. The six-case numerical checker checks finite identities but does not certify infinite asymptotics.

value.rationale: The 2026 motivating paper leaves the cusp distance estimates quantitatively open. An exact leading axial metric coefficient, and the resulting exact intrinsic-axis length coefficient, resolve a natural computable portion of that gap, distinguish it from ambient distance, and demonstrate a nontrivial double saddle-point mechanism for a superpolynomially vanishing fiber. This is neither a routine weight substitution nor an arbitrary finite parameter slice.
